latest.text:
Zverev beat Jodar in straight sets in the opening singles match of the week in Turin, against a 20-year-old who was playing the event for the first time.

It was not easy for either of them. The ball was not flying through the air on this fast indoor court and both players seemed to struggle at times to control it. Jodar held well early on but Zverev broke him late in the first set and served for it. Jodar had two break points in that game, the only chances he got all match and Zverev saved both to take the set 6–4. The second set followed the same pattern. Zverev broke early, did not see another break point and took it 6–4 as well.

That serve was the whole story, because Jodar barely got a look at it. Zverev won 86% of the points behind his first serve, against his 74% average on hard. He was also the more clutch of the two on the big points.

It was not perfect but it did not need to be. It was not his best return performance and he let most of his break points go. Still, one break in each set was enough and the moment that decided it came when he held while serving for the first set. Shelton waits in his next match.

latest.text:
Fritz beat Tirante 6–2, 4–6, 7–6 in the Stockholm final to win his first indoor title, the 12th of his career.

Fritz broke early after some strong defence to take the first set 6–2 but Tirante came back with attacking tennis and one break gave him the second 6–4. Fritz saw it the same way: "It was a stressful match, … I came out and was playing really well but then let some opportunities slip." Nobody was broken in the third set and Fritz, now finding his forehand, was the better player in the tiebreak and took it 7–3.

His serve held up through all of it, even the second serve: he won 73% of the points behind it, far above his average of 53% on hard.

On the other side, Tirante, who called the physio in the SF, did not call for a medical timeout this time.

All in all, a deserved title built on a strong start and a serve that held in the third set, the strengths of a big server and complete baseliner like Fritz in these indoor conditions. He said: "It feels, it feels nice."

commentary.text: Fritz won the Stockholm final against Tirante in three sets, taking his first indoor title and the 12th title of his career. Fritz broke early in the first set after some strong defence and played well in that set but Tirante improved and took the second set to force a deciding set. Tirante played aggressive, attacking tennis and came to the net often, winning several points with his volleys, though some volleys were not good enough. Fritz hit some powerful returns and found his forehand more and more often as the match went on and he returned to his first-set level to close it out. Tirante, playing in his first final, pushed Fritz all the way and Fritz's experience may have made the difference.
